items.title: Lifting an inverse system of objects of D(Ab) to a system of complexes whose transition diagrams commute strictly
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement compares an inverse system (K_n) of objects of the derived category D(Ab), which is not the same thing as a system of complexes, with a system of complexes whose transition diagrams commute strictly; it asserts that every such inverse system in D(Ab) can be represented by an object of D(Ab(N)) together with levelwise isomorphisms making the diagrams commute in D(Ab) (statement lines 23334-23348). The proof is an induction on the length of the system in which the nontrivial step is the construction of the next transition map: one has to realize the composite of the given map K_{n+1} -> K_n with the inverse of the chosen isomorphism as an honest morphism of complexes, and this is exactly what the definition of morphisms in D(Ab) provides (proof lines 23356-23371). The diagram is a diagram in D(Ab) and is displayed with Xy-pic in the author's markup. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing.
